sources.title: Bajo la sequía y la incertidumbre, son las mujeres quienes sostienen la alimentación del hogar
sources.temporal_coverage: WFP field story published July 2026, describing recent rainfall, harvest and household food-access conditions.
sources.methodology: WFP country-programme field story with a named household case.
sources.limitations: Qualitative case reporting; it does not estimate population-wide effects or independently evaluate the grain bank.

sources.title: SESAN presenta pronóstico de inseguridad alimentaria para el período 2026-2027 y acciones de respuesta
sources.organization: Secretariat for Food and Nutrition Security of the Presidency of Guatemala (SESAN)
sources.temporal_coverage: Government IPC acute-food-insecurity forecast announced August 2026 for July 2026–February 2027.
sources.methodology: Government page summarizing a multi-institutional Integrated Food Security Phase Classification analysis.
sources.limitations: Dated forecasts, not verified outcomes; July–September had elapsed by access date.

sources.title: Fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de los hogares en el corredor seco de Guatemala para vivir mejor
sources.temporal_coverage: Joint programme runs March 2022–December 2026; page includes programme design context and planned outputs.
sources.methodology: UNDP project profile describing target area, context and planned outputs.
sources.limitations: Dated design context; outputs are targets, not evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Guatemala: Acute Food Insecurity Situation for April–June 2026 and Projections for July 2026–February 2027
sources.temporal_coverage: IPC acute food-insecurity analysis valid April 2026–February 2027, released August 2026.
sources.methodology: Directly opened IPC country-analysis page reporting phase classifications, population estimates and recommendations.
sources.limitations: The page's accessible narrative gives national estimates; the linked report PDF was not inspected and no department-level classification is asserted here.

claims.paraphrase: WFP reports that climate variability compounded by El Niño is reducing Dry Corridor harvests and food access, with women bearing a disproportionate household food-allocation burden.
claims.limitations: WFP's qualitative report concerns the 2026 episode and does not attribute the natural El Niño event to anthropogenic climate change.

claims.paraphrase: In Uriles Pinalón, Jalapa, a woman farmer described late, insufficient rain and poor milpa yields; WFP says women in rural Indigenous communities, including Ch’orti’-speaking areas, often reduce their own food portions for household members.
claims.limitations: The named account is one community case; the article does not quantify the prevalence of reduced consumption by place.

claims.paraphrase: WFP reports installing a CERF-supported grain bank and silo in Uriles Pinalón; local women organize and manage the grain, reducing the need for households to travel to town to buy maize and beans.
claims.limitations: WFP's case story describes an operating intervention but does not independently measure its reach or effects.

claims.paraphrase: SESAN forecast 3.2 million people (17%) in Phase 3 or above in July–September 2026, citing probable El Niño drought and food and transport inflation.
claims.scenario: SESAN forecast probable El Niño effects; no emissions scenario was stated. The period elapsed before access; outcome unverified.
affected_groups: people in IPC Phase 3 or above
claims.limitations: This records a dated forecast, not the measured July–September result.

claims.paraphrase: The July–September forecast classified Alta Verapaz in Phase 3; ten named departments across the Western Highlands and Dry Corridor were forecast to have 15–19% of residents in Phase 3 or worse, associated with poverty, subsistence farming and limited services.
claims.scenario: SESAN July–September 2026 forecast; no emissions scenario stated. Period elapsed; result unverified.
claims.limitations: Forecast shares, not measured outcomes; page does not identify municipalities.

claims.locator: Project overview and coverage, lines 31–32 and 38–51.
claims.paraphrase: The UN joint programme targets more than 7,000 households, especially children under five and pregnant or lactating women, in seven Dry Corridor municipalities across Chiquimula and Jalapa: Jocotán, Camotán, Olopa, San Juan Ermita, Chiquimula, San Luis Jilotepeque and San Pedro Pinula.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Food
claims.limitations: These are programme targets and design, not independently evaluated outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: The project profile identifies irregular rainfall, drought, floods, landslides, environmental degradation and low crop yields in its Dry Corridor context; it reports that Indigenous people, especially women and children, are disproportionately affected by poverty and social exclusion.
claims.limitations: Dated programme context, including cited FAO 2020 material; poverty data are not updated here.

claims.paraphrase: Planned outputs include drought-adapted food systems, community water infrastructure and watershed planning with women's participation, plus stronger central and local capacity for food and water security and gender-responsive resilience.
claims.limitations: The profile lists intended results; it does not establish that the outputs or capacity changes were achieved.

claims.locator: IPC analysis page, key results, lines 73–75.
claims.paraphrase: The IPC analysis estimated 2.5 million people in Phase 3 or above in April–June 2026; it forecast 3.2 million for July–September as the lean season and anticipated El Niño effects constrained access, then 2.6 million for October 2026–February 2027 as harvests and seasonal work improved.
claims.scenario: The IPC's 2026 forecast used a lean-season and anticipated El Niño outlook; no emissions scenario stated. The July–September period had elapsed by access date; outcomes were not verified.
affected_groups: people in IPC Phase 3 or above
claims.limitations: The accessible page gives national estimates; projections are not outcomes and detailed report PDF was not inspected.
